title: You can't beat AI: why judgment, taste and systems replace average work
summary: Ruben argues AI makes intelligence a cheap commodity, so average work dies first and the market stops paying for it. Durable value shifts to judgment and taste, which you must extract into reusable context files, and to building repeatable systems rather than selling hours or answers.

principles.text: The threat isn't perfect AI, it's AI cheap enough to replace 'good enough'.
principles.quote: The threat is not that AI becomes perfect. The threat is that AI becomes cheap enough to replace good enough.

principles.text: When intelligence gets cheap, judgment gets expensive: the valuable person picks, decides and spots what matters.
principles.quote: When intelligence gets cheap, judgment gets expensive.

principles.text: Stop making average work; average now looks suspicious because it took seconds. Move above it.
principles.quote: Stop trying to make average work. Move above it.

principles.text: Turn your taste and expertise into reusable markdown context files so AI stops giving average answers.
principles.quote: A prompt is a one-time request. But a file (inside a folder) is reusable memory.

principles.text: Move from answer person to system person: build templates and workflows so you remove bottlenecks.
principles.quote: You stop being the bottleneck. You remove bottlenecks.

principles.text: Use AI where you already have taste, because you can't judge output in areas where you're weak.
principles.quote: If you’re bad at the thing, you can’t judge the thing.
